goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P1, confidence 100, defect] `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` duplicate or case-variant rows are representable because `host` has no normalized UNIQUE constraint, so saving the same hostname against two categories makes lookup choose an arbitrary category and the unindexed expression scans the whole table on every embed request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: the EmbeddableHost model has no unique constraint on the host column (as seen in the migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb which only creates a non-null constraint). The lookup method `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. Additionally, there's no index on the host column, meaning every embed request will do a full table scan. However, the severity is somewhat overstated - the admin UI would need to allow creating duplicates first, and the table is likely small. The lack of index and unique constraint is a real defect that could cause incorrect category assignment and performance issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — [P1, confidence 100, defect] `host = uri.host` a configured value containing the explicitly accepted `:port` suffix never matches because URI extraction drops the port while the persisted lookup key retains it, so every request for that configured host is rejected and its topics are never routed to the selected category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the EmbeddableHost model: the validation regex allows ports (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the before_validation strips the protocol and path but NOT the port from the host field. However, in `record_for_host`, `uri.host` is used which returns only the hostname without the port (URI parsing separates host and port). So if an admin configures 'example.com:8080', it's stored as 'example.com:8080', but when checking `host_allowed?`, the lookup uses `uri.host` which returns 'example.com' (without port), causing the WHERE clause `lower(host) = 'example.com'` to not match 'example.com:8080'. This is a legitimate correctness bug.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration creates category_id as NOT NULL without a foreign key constraint. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has `belongs_to :category` but there's no foreign key constraint in the migration, and the controller (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb) accepts any category_id from params. If a category is deleted, the embeddable_host records would have orphaned category_ids. The model validation only checks host format, not category existence. This is a real data integrity issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — [P1, confidence 100, defect] `delete obj[k];` every REST-serialized plural foreign-key field is now destructively rewritten even when its related collection was not sideloaded, so a payload containing any legitimate `*_ids` array without embedded records loses its authoritative IDs and exposes an array of unresolved values to all downstream consumers.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in store.js.es6 lines 189-212, the new code handles `*_ids` fields (plural). When `m[2]` is truthy (meaning it matched `_ids`), it maps over `obj[k]` to hydrate each id, then unconditionally does `delete obj[k]` regardless of whether hydration succeeded. The hydrated array is assigned to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` with `|| []` fallback, but if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined/null for each id (because the related records weren't sideloaded), the original `*_ids` array is still deleted. This means legitimate `*_ids` arrays are destroyed even when their related records aren't in the payload, losing the authoritative ID data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — [P2, confidence 100, defect] `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` saving a new host without choosing a category makes the server assign uncategorized but then overwrites the returned association from the stale null client field, so the persisted row and displayed/editable state disagree until a full reload.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the save action. Looking at lines 29-38 of embeddable-host.js.es6, when saving a host: (1) props.category_id is set from this.get('categoryId'), (2) host.save(props) is called, (3) in the .then() callback, host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))) is executed. The problem is that categoryId can be null (initialized as null on line 9), and the server-side code in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 23-24 shows it defaults to uncategorized_category_id when category_id is blank. So the server assigns a valid category, but the client immediately overwrites the host's category with Category.findById(null), which would return undefined/null, causing the displayed state to disagree with the persisted state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — [P2, confidence 100, defect] `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z` configuring a valid hostname whose top-level domain exceeds five characters is rejected, so hosts on modern domains such as `.technology` cannot use the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new regex validation in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Modern TLDs like `.technology` (10 chars), `.photography` (11 chars), etc. would be rejected by this validation. This is a real defect that prevents legitimate hostnames from being configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:18 — [P3, confidence 75, advisory] `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` the admin endpoint materializes and serializes the entire externally growable host set into one table, so configuration growth makes response size, server memory, hydration work, and DOM size increase without bound; the expectation that installations keep the list small does not survive the absence of either a cap or pagination, and deleting this eager aggregate in favor of a paged host resource removes the synthetic embedding update endpoint and the global plural-ID hydration branch.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is a scalability issue because the endpoint loads all embeddable hosts without pagination. However, this is an admin configuration endpoint for managing embedding hosts - a feature that by design would have a small, bounded number of entries (typically single digits to low tens of allowed embedding domains). The diff shows this is a new admin UI for managing embeddable hosts, replacing a previous site setting approach. The claim that this 'removes the synthetic embedding update endpoint and the global plural-ID hydration branch' is confusing and doesn't match what the code does. This is a reasonable design for an admin configuration page, not a scalability bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P1, confidence 100, defect] `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` Saving the same normalized hostname against two categories creates multiple valid rows because no uniqueness constraint exists, so an embed selects an arbitrary relationship and posts into the wrong category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new EmbeddableHost model lacks a uniqueness constraint on the host column. Looking at the migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the table is created with just 'host' and 'category_id' columns but no unique index on host. The model in app/models/embeddable_host.rb only has a format validation but no uniqueness validation. adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the migration. Looking at line 19 of the migration: `if embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. For SELECT statements in PostgreSQL via ActiveRecord's execute, `cmd_tuples` returns the number of rows affected by the last command, but for SELECT it typically returns 0 (it's meant for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). The correct check should use `.count` or check the result set directly.
